title: Leaving for Chicago in 1929 and hearing the New Orleans men there
summary: He went to Chicago alone in 1929 and auditioned for Decca. He heard Louis Armstrong at the Sunset and Oliver at the Plantation and was nervous when asked to sit in.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: You played around New Orleans for quite a few years. Do you remember just when you left? Yeah, I left in 29. That is to go to Chicago. I mean was that on your own hook or did you? No, it was on my own. Did you bring a band with you? No, I left by myself. And what did you do in Chicago? Form a band?
Well, I had to play in with different combinations and I had a chance to audition for some recording. What company was that? That was Decker.
Well, you say you got Chicago in 29. Yeah. Now, were there many New Orleans musicians in Chicago at the time? Oh yeah, there was quite a few there. Could you name a few that you knew?

Well, it was like Lewis, he was at Sunset at the time, and Dublin at the Van Dooms here on State Street, and Oliver, he was at the Plantation on 35th Street, and that was my first chance to hear them away from home. And they really treated me well. Lewis even asked me to play a song to do a number at the sunset. That band was too great. I felt kind of shaky sitting up there with great musicians like that.
